correctness.rationale: For every finite tensor product with local dimension >=2 and weights positive summing to one, direct Kraus normalization proves CPTP. Site maps commute and are idempotent. Conditioning on the visited set writes T^m=(1-p)R+pN with CPTP N, giving a diamond upper bound 2p. A tensor product of states orthogonal at each site to the target is orthogonal to the target after every incomplete update history, saturating both the system-state trace distance and diamond norm. Inclusion–exclusion proves the weighted finite formula for all m>=0 (0^0=1). A uniform factorial-series domination justifies the Gumbel cutoff and its epsilon quantile. Walsh/Fourier chi-square upper and magnetization Chebyshev lower bounds give classical mixing time (1/2+o(1))n log n. The packaged verify.py completed 122 direct Kraus, independent subset-mask, ancilla-reference, biased qubit–qutrit and finite asymptotic tests. The experiments are not used as infinite-size proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement is an exact operational diamond-norm equality, valid with arbitrary entangled references, for nonuniform product-state quantum refresh channels, together with the all-time inclusion–exclusion law and a sharp uniform Gumbel cutoff. Temme–Wocjan (arXiv:2504.02651v1 and published version) provide the underlying quantized grand-coupling formula and the classical hypercube coupon upper tail, but not the matching quantum distinguishability witness or the strong norm equality. The classical coupon and hypercube cutoff are established and explicitly credited. Searches and statement-level comparisons found no stronger result implying the exact formula. Earlier unindexed or implicitly obtainable derivations remain a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: The identity may be an unindexed or implicitly observed consequence of prior reset-channel algebra, despite no covering statement in the inspected relevant manuscripts.
A more general theorem about commuting idempotent channels might imply this case even without similar vocabulary; the targeted searches did not find one.
The classical hypercube-cutoff paper was available in abstract only; the classical comparison is separately proved from Walsh analysis here.
The exact law does not extend to arbitrary grand-coupling quantum channels; the authors’ general prefactor problem remains open.

value.rationale: The natural product-refresh qsample family was studied with only nonsharp generic bounds; the new exact operational diamond norm provides a reference-ancilla-safe benchmark at every finite time and arbitrary site weights. The uniform sharp Gumbel window and time-quantile law identify the precise mixing cost without an exponentially small stationary probability penalty. The explicit ratio two against the matched classical hypercube TV cutoff distinguishes coherent preparation from classical sampling and gives an interpretable exact performance threshold. The result is scoped to commuting pure replacement maps; broad prefactor conjectures are not claimed.
